program_name: Food Science and Technology - curriculum in Food Systems (official UNITO full name: 'Master Degree in Food Science and Technology, curriculum in Food Systems'; Italian catalogue name: 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari (curriculum in Food Systems)'). Marketed internationally as the EIT Food 'Master in Food Systems' (MFS) with University of Turin as one of the degree-awarding partners. [uncertain]
teaching_language: Fully English-taught, but NOT a stand-alone English degree: it is an English-language curriculum ('curriculum in Food Systems') inside the Italian-named second-cycle degree 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari' (LM-70). The UNITO microsite states 'Language: English' for the whole curriculum (2 years, 120 ECTS). It is also an INTERUNIVERSITY / consortium programme: the EIT Food Master in Food Systems is delivered by a consortium of European universities (University of Turin, University of Hohenheim, University of Warsaw, Lund University, Aarhus University, Universidad CEU San Pablo, University of Reading), and a student on a UNITO-based path spends only part of the four semesters in Turin (e.g. UNITO-LU-UW: sem.1 Turin, sem.2 Lund, sem.3 Warsaw, sem.4 thesis Turin; UNITO-UHOH is run as a DUAL DEGREE). Note that the SAME LM-70 degree also has a separate 'curriculum Tradizionale', which Apply@UniTo describes as 'combined Italian/English' - that traditional curriculum is a different, largely Italian-language track and must not be confused with the English Food Systems curriculum.
campus: Turin, Italy - Department of Agricultural, Forest and Food Sciences (DISAFA), Largo Paolo Braccini 2, Grugliasco (Turin metropolitan area). Because the programme is a mobility-based consortium degree, one or two semesters are spent at the partner universities abroad (Lund - Sweden, Warsaw - Poland, Hohenheim/Stuttgart - Germany, Aarhus - Denmark, depending on the chosen path); the thesis semester is at UNITO or, for the UNITO-UHOH dual-degree path, at Hohenheim.
degree_class: LM-70 - Scienze e tecnologie alimentari / Food Science and Technology. UNITO internal degree-programme code: 010503; regulated under Italian ministerial decree D.M. 270. UNITO institutional catalogue page for the English degree: en.unito.it/ugov/degree/39785.
admission_type: Selection call (competitive, consortium-run selection), NOT an Italian TOLC/SAT test and not a simple first-come open-access enrolment. Applications for the Food Systems curriculum are submitted through the EIT Food consortium portal mfs-apply.eitfood.eu (DreamApply), where the candidate may select up to three preferred study paths; the applications are reviewed by the universities in those paths and shortlisted candidates are invited to an online (or face-to-face) interview. Admission is granted per intake round; accepted students then pay a deposit and enrol at UNITO. On the UNITO side the underlying LM-70 degree 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari' is administratively an open-access ('libero accesso') postgraduate degree with verification of personal preparation, and Apply@UniTo records a territorial quota of 50 places reserved to non-EU applicants residing abroad, shared among ALL curricula of Scienze e tecnologie alimentari. The Apply@UniTo course page for the Food Systems curriculum (course 678) explicitly redirects applicants: 'Apply at: mfs-apply.eitfood.eu'. [uncertain]
application_deadline_eu: For the 2026 intake (studies starting autumn 2026, i.e. academic year 2026/2027) the EIT Food MFS calendar had three rounds: 1st intake - 31 January 2026 (all candidates); 2nd intake - 30 March 2026 (all candidates); 3rd intake - 25 June 2026, valid for EU/EEA candidates (DreamApply territory list: EU countries plus United Kingdom, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway). EU/EEA applicants for UNITO-based paths could therefore apply up to 25 June 2026. Results announced mid-end February / mid-end April / end June-mid July respectively. NOTE: as of the research date (1 September 2026) these 2026 rounds are closed and the equivalent 2027-intake deadlines had not yet been published. The (now expired) Apply@UniTo record for course 678 listed only a 30 March 2025 worldwide deadline for a.y. 2025/26. [uncertain]
application_deadline_non_eu: For the 2026 intake (a.y. 2026/2027), non-EU/EEA applicants who want a UNITO-based path had to apply in the 1st intake (deadline 31 January 2026) or the 2nd intake (deadline 30 March 2026). The 3rd intake (25 June 2026) was open to non-EU/EEA citizens ONLY for paths starting at the University of Warsaw or the University of Hohenheim, so it was not available for UNITO-starting paths. In addition, non-EU citizens residing abroad who need a study visa must complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment application for a.y. 2026/2027 by 15 July 2026 (UNITO general rule, referenced from the programme's 'Pre-enrolment' page). Deadlines for the 2027 intake were not yet published at the research date. [uncertain]
entry_exam_or_test: No written entrance examination, no TOLC, no GRE/GMAT. Selection is document-based plus an interview: the UNITO 'Selection criteria' page states that the application is evaluated on (1) the final grade of the undergraduate degree, (2) experience in the field of entrepreneurship or subject-related experience, and (3) an interview lasting approximately 30 minutes, in which the candidate first introduces themselves and their motivation for the programme (to assess entrepreneurial potential) and is then asked questions about the food system related to the fields of expertise of the universities selected in the application. The UNITO 'Admission requirements' page confirms: 'An on-line or face to face interview will take place to assess your suitability to the program.' Only shortlisted candidates are invited to the interview. [uncertain]
academic_requirements: Entry qualification: a first-cycle university degree (Bachelor's diploma or higher, at least 3 years / 180 ECTS or equivalent) recognised by the regulations in force. Eligible bachelor fields listed by UNITO: Agricultural Sciences; Food Sciences (food technology, safety, quality); Biology; Chemistry; Biotechnology; Pharmacy; Veterinary Science; Nutritional Science. The consortium admission page adds Food Safety, Nutrition and/or Economics and Management, and states that 'relevant degrees in other fields may be considered by the admissions committee on a case-by-case basis'. Path-specific academic prerequisites also apply, e.g. for the UNITO-starting tracks: Track/Semester 1 (UNITO, 'Food safety of the whole value chain') requires basic knowledge of food microbiology; other semesters require basic knowledge of the food system and, for engineering/science-heavy tracks, basic science or engineering knowledge (food, agriculture, natural sciences such as biology, chemistry or biotechnology, or chemical/mechanical/process engineering). Soft-skill expectation stated by UNITO: 'Interest in research and development of food processes and entrepreneurial spirit.' No numerical GPA threshold is published, but the final grade of the bachelor's degree is one of the three official selection criteria. Applicants may select up to three study paths in one application. Places/quotas: Apply@UniTo records 50 places reserved for non-EU applicants residing abroad for the LM-70 degree, shared across all its curricula (original Italian wording: 'Questo corso di laurea magistrale ha a disposizione 50 posti riservati a candidati non-EU residenti all'estero. Questi posti sono in comune con tutti i curricula di Scienze e tecnologie alimentari'); EIT Food additionally offers 50 scholarships for EU & UK citizens and 50 for non-EU citizens per intake. A specific numerus clausus for the Food Systems curriculum itself is not published. [uncertain]
language_requirements: English at minimum CEFR B2 level, documented. Accepted evidence per the UNITO programme page and the consortium admission-requirements page: (a) TOEFL internet-based with at least 90 points; (b) IELTS Academic with at least 6.5 overall and at least 5.5 in each of written production, oral production, listening comprehension and reading comprehension; (c) a Bachelor's or Master's diploma from a programme studied entirely in English as the medium of instruction, accepted only for recognised institutions in: all EU countries or Switzerland; United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, New Zealand, USA; Antigua and Barbuda, Bahamas, Barbados, Dominica, Grenada, Jamaica, St. Kitts and Nevis, St. Lucia, St. Vincent and the Grenadines, Trinidad and Tobago, Belize, Guyana. Other proofs of B2 or higher may be evaluated by the admissions committee case by case, and path-specific requirements should always be checked. No Italian-language requirement is set for admission (the curriculum is entirely in English). Special rule for paths that include a track in the United Kingdom: a UK study visa requires a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from the UK Visas & Immigration approved list; applicants may apply without it but cannot fully enrol until it is provided (not applicable to purely UNITO/EU paths). Note that the OTHER curriculum of the same LM-70 degree (curriculum Tradizionale, Apply@UniTo course 222) requires knowledge of BOTH Italian and English, verified in the admission interview - that requirement does not apply to the English Food Systems curriculum.
required_documents: Application (submitted on mfs-apply.eitfood.eu, DreamApply): (1) entry qualification documents - Bachelor's diploma/degree certificate and transcript of records; the UNITO admission-requirements page accepts them in English or Italian, while the consortium course pages state English; if issued in another language, official translations together with verified copies of the originals must be uploaded, and originals must be brought to the university at enrolment; (2) documented proof of English proficiency at B2 or above (TOEFL iBT >=90, IELTS Academic >=6.5, or an English-taught degree from the accepted country list, or other evidence accepted case by case); (3) selection of up to three preferred study paths in the online application form; (4) participation in an online/in-person interview if shortlisted; (5) for paths including a UK track, a UKVI-approved SELT certificate before full enrolment; (6) after an offer is accepted, payment of the non-refundable deposit within 7 days. Enrolment stage at UNITO: registration on the UNITO portal and the documents listed in UNITO's separate EU / non-EU enrolment instructions; non-EU citizens residing abroad must additionally complete the Universitaly pre-enrolment application and obtain a study visa (UNITO deadline for a.y. 2026/2027: 15 July 2026), and are normally asked for the legalised qualification with a Declaration of Value / CIMEA Statement of Comparability, plus passport/identity document. A CV and a motivation letter are commonly part of the DreamApply form, but no official public page listing them item by item could be retrieved, so the application-form document list is reported as reconstructed rather than quoted. [uncertain]

uncertainty_notes: 1) PROGRAMME IDENTITY / NAMING. The outline entry 'Food Science and Technology' with the URL www.mfs.unito.it does NOT correspond to a stand-alone English degree of that name. mfs.unito.it is the microsite of the 'Master Degree in Food Science and Technology, curriculum in Food Systems' - i.e. the English-taught FOOD SYSTEMS CURRICULUM inside the Italian LM-70 degree 'Scienze e tecnologie alimentari'. The same LM-70 degree also has a 'curriculum Tradizionale' (Apply@UniTo course 222) which is listed as 'combined Italian/English' and requires Italian as well as English; that traditional curriculum is NOT English-taught and has completely different admission rules (open-access UNITO call, deadline 8 September 2026 for EU/legally-resident applicants, evaluation interview on food microbiology/technology/engineering/economics/chemistry, at least 60 ECTS of prior credits in maths, physics, chemistry, food engineering, food microbiology, food technology, microsite stal.unito.it). All data in this record refer to the ENGLISH Food Systems curriculum. If the ItalyPath entry is meant to describe the whole LM-70 degree, the language field must be treated as mixed. 2) INTERUNIVERSITY / MOBILITY. This is a consortium programme (EIT Food Master in Food Systems). A student does not spend all four semesters in Turin, and one UNITO path (UNITO-UHOH) is a dual degree with the University of Hohenheim. Applications are not processed by Apply@UniTo but by the consortium portal mfs-apply.eitfood.eu; the Apply@UniTo course page (678) exists mainly as a catalogue record and explicitly says 'Apply at: mfs-apply.eitfood.eu'. Because of this, several sources cited here are on mfs-apply.eitfood.eu / learning.eitfood.eu rather than on unito.it; they are the official portal that UNITO itself points to, but they are not unito.it domains. Where a fact exists on both, the unito.it version has been quoted. 3) ACCESS LIMITATIONS. www.mfs.unito.it refuses direct connections from this environment (ECONNREFUSED on 130.186.3.24), and en.unito.it / www.unito.it return 403; the archive.org availability API repeatedly returned HTTP 429. All mfs.unito.it content quoted here therefore comes from Internet Archive raw ('id_') captures: Key informations = 18 June 2024 capture (page last updated 06/09/2023), Admission requirements = 19 May 2025 capture (page last updated 23/07/2024), How to apply / Tuition fees = captures of pages last updated 23-24/07/2024, Selection criteria = 2023 capture of a page last updated 13/07/2020, Pre-enrolment = capture of a page last updated 24/07/2024. The live 2026/27 wording on the microsite could not be read, so the academic and language requirements are reported as of the most recent retrievable official text; they are corroborated by the currently live consortium admission-requirements page, which matches word for word on the B2/TOEFL 90/IELTS 6.5 rules and the eligible bachelor fields. 4) DEADLINES AND CYCLE. Research date is 1 September 2026, so the 2026 intake (studies starting autumn 2026 = a.y. 2026/2027) is already closed and the 2027-intake calendar was not yet published. The three 2026 deadlines are taken from the consortium news item (which prints day and month only) cross-checked against the machine-readable JSON feed of the UNITO-based courses, which gives the explicit dates 2026-01-31, 2026-03-30 and 2026-06-25 with the EU/GB/IS/LI/NO territory restriction on the last round. The Apply@UniTo record for course 678 is stale (status 'Standby', last updated 19 November 2024) and still shows only the a.y. 2025/26 deadline of 30 March 2025 plus an outdated 250 EUR deposit. 5) NON-EU QUOTA. The figure of 50 places reserved for non-EU applicants residing abroad comes from the Apply@UniTo page of the Tradizionale curriculum, which states the places are shared among all curricula of Scienze e tecnologie alimentari; the Food Systems course page itself does not restate it, and it is unclear in practice how that ministerial quota interacts with the consortium's own selection, so it should not be read as a cap on Food Systems admissions. No dedicated numerus clausus for the Food Systems curriculum is published. 6) REQUIRED DOCUMENTS. No official page enumerates the full DreamApply upload checklist for this programme; the list given is assembled from the entry-qualification and language-requirement wording on the UNITO and consortium pages plus the acceptance/deposit and UNITO enrolment steps. Whether a CV, motivation letter or reference letters are separately mandatory in the online form could not be confirmed from an official source. 7) PATH LIST CHANGES YEARLY. The set of UNITO-based paths changes between intakes (the archived UNITO page lists older combinations such as UNITO-UAM-AU and UNITO-QUB-UHOH that no longer appear); for the 2026 intake the live UNITO-starting paths were UNITO-LU-UW, UNITO-UW-AU and UNITO-UHOH (dual degree), plus paths where UNITO hosts a middle semester. Prospective applicants must check the path list for the intake year they apply to. 8) FEES. The 9,000 EUR (EU) / 18,000 EUR (non-EU) participation fee is a consortium fee and is NOT the ordinary UNITO tuition contribution; scholarship holders pay reduced amounts, and Type Q scholarships can lower an EU student's fee to the home university's regular tuition. UNITO's ordinary tuition-fee regulation pages are given for reference only.
